status_detail: First phase is live on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure; Crusoe says construction began in June 2024, first two buildings energized within a year, and campus expansion to 1.2GW continues.
notes: Flagship Stargate site; Oracle is cloud/platform lessee for OpenAI workloads. A separately discussed expansion beyond 1.2GW has reportedly shifted to Microsoft/other tenants, so this entry records the core 1.2GW campus.

status_detail: Vantage announced a $25B 1.4GW campus in August 2025; later reporting and Vantage materials tie Frontier to Stargate/OpenAI-Oracle and show groundbreaking/construction activity.
notes: Vantage states 10 data centers across roughly 1,200 acres; external capacity estimates vary up to 2GW, but primary Vantage disclosure says 1.4GW.

status_detail: OpenAI selected SB Energy to build and operate a previously announced 1.2GW data center site in Milam County; SB Energy lists the Milam Data Center as under construction.
notes: DCD/Texas filing coverage identifies the first phase as Freebird, about 548,950 sq ft; Cleanview tracks Building 1 at 300MW expected 2027.

status_detail: Aligned announced groundbreaking on a 540MW, 313-acre, six-facility campus outside Abernathy, with inaugural data center LBB-01 anticipated in Q1 2027.
notes: Company FAQ says 1.65M sq ft across six facilities.

developer: Fermi America; Texas Tech University System
status_detail: Fermi plans an up-to-11GW data center and energy campus on Texas Tech land near Amarillo; DCD reported preliminary approval for 6GW gas generation and multiple turbine/pipeline/nuclear-prep deals. Barron's reported TensorWave as first tenant on August 11, 2026, with rights to expand above 650MW.
notes: Very large early-stage campus; 11GW is planned total including gas, nuclear, solar, wind, batteries and grid power. Tenant lease starts in second half 2027 per news report.

project_name: GW Ranch / Amazon Pecos County Campus
status_detail: Amazon acquired the 8,000-acre GW Ranch site from Pacifico Energy and plans a behind-the-meter data center campus; TCEQ permit allows up to 7.65GW of gas generation, with solar and battery options.
notes: Capacity is power-generation/private-grid permit capacity; actual IT load not separately disclosed. Pacifico page says construction can start Q1 2026 with first power Q1 2027.

status_detail: Microsoft announced a new Pecos datacenter campus adding approximately 2GW of capacity; Chevron/Engine No. 1 will supply up to 2.67GW behind the meter under Project Kirby, with first power expected in 2028.
notes: Pecos city is in Reeves County; Cleanview separately tracks Microsoft Pecos Data Center in Reeves.

status_detail: LandBridge and PowerBridge signed a lease development agreement for up to roughly 3,400 acres in Reeves County and up to 2GW of initial co-located power generation; later Liberty/PowerBridge JV coverage says initial phase over 300MW with power from Q4 2027.
notes: Private-use power network near Waha hub; early commercial/lease option stage.

developer: Poolside AI; formerly CoreWeave as anchor tenant
status_detail: Poolside announced a 2GW AI campus on the Longfellow Ranch/near Fort Stockton, initially with CoreWeave as anchor tenant for 250MW expandable to 500MW; DCD later reported CoreWeave dropped out and Poolside is seeking partners.
notes: Retained as early announcement despite anchor-tenant change; separate from Amazon/GW Ranch unless later evidence proves consolidation.

project_name: Amazon Fort Stockton Data Center Campus
status_detail: Amazon filed Texas construction applications for a three-building campus near Fort Stockton; reports cite three 189,000 sq ft buildings with roughly $300M cost each and construction beginning in August 2026.
notes: May overlap with Amazon's GW Ranch acquisition; kept as a separate permit-level clue because the DCD filing story lists Fort Stockton as one of two new campuses.

status_detail: DCD reported Amazon filed applications to develop new data center buildings across two Texas campuses, including Floydada.
notes: Early permit/application-stage project; building count and capacity not fully separated in public reporting.

status_detail: DCD reported Amazon filed to expand a planned campus in Boling with six more buildings while also filing for Fort Stockton and Floydada campuses.
notes: Expansion of a planned AWS campus; listed separately because it is a distinct city/county from the new West Texas filings.

status_detail: Google lists Midlothian as one of its Texas data center locations; DCD reported a fifth building filing at 3441 Railport Parkway, same Midlothian campus, in 2026.
notes: Capacity shown from tracker; official Google page confirms location but not MW. Fifth building expansion is under filing/construction pipeline.

project_name: Google Red Oak Data Center Campus
status_detail: Google lists Red Oak as a Texas data center location; DCD reported the $600M Red Oak campus announcement in 2023, and Cleanview tracks Building 1 as operating in 2025 at 107MW.
notes: Red Oak has additional local rezoning/development activity nearby; this entry records Google's named campus.

status_detail: Google announced new Texas data center campuses including Armstrong County; later coverage identifies the Armstrong project as Goodnight and links it to a planned 933MW gas plant for part of the campus.
notes: Capacity is associated power plant figure from news, not official IT load. Google official source confirms Armstrong campus but not the Goodnight details.

status_detail: Google announced two Haskell County data center campuses as part of its $40B Texas cloud/AI infrastructure investment through 2027.
notes: Texas Tribune and CoStar say Google will build three new data centers: one in Armstrong and two in Haskell.

project_name: Google Haskell County Campus with Solar and Battery
status_detail: One of Google's two Haskell County data centers is reported to be paired with new solar and battery storage to reduce grid impact.
notes: Separated from the other Haskell entry because public reporting describes two Haskell data centers and specific energy pairing for one.

project_name: Google Meitner Energy Center / Pampa Data Center
status_detail: Google and Intersect announced construction of the Meitner Energy Center, including a new co-located data center and energy generation in Gray and Roberts Counties near Pampa.
notes: Project spans Gray and Roberts Counties; county field uses Gray because public local coverage places the data center near Pampa/Gray County. MW not disclosed for data center.

status_detail: Google's Texas data center location page says 2026 campus developments include Pampa and Wilbarger Counties; Power Magazine also notes Wilbarger County near Vernon as under construction.
notes: Early public detail is limited; retained as named county-level Google project.

project_name: Hut 8 Beacon Point AI Data Center Campus
status_detail: Hut 8 announced commercialization of first phase at Beacon Point through a 15-year lease for 352MW IT capacity and has a 1GW interconnection agreement; initial energization expected Q1 2027 and preliminary data hall delivery Q3 2027.
notes: DCD describes 525-acre campus near Corpus Christi; phase capacity leased is 352MW, total interconnection 1GW.

developer: Texas Critical Data Centers; New Era Energy & Digital; Sharon AI
status_detail: TCDC closed on 235 acres in Ector County for an AI data center initially expected at 250MW with potential to scale beyond 1GW; later Energy Dome release says the master-planned campus spans 438 acres outside Odessa.
notes: Early off-grid/energy-integrated AI campus; possible expansion to 1GW+ noted but 250MW is the announced initial capacity.

project_name: SB Energy Borden County Data Center Campus
aliases: SB Energy Global Data Center Campus
status_detail: SB Energy lists a Borden County Data Center Campus with total capacity of 1GW+ and status 'In Early Construction.'
notes: Limited public project detail; retained because developer's own digital infrastructure page identifies the Borden County campus.

project_name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center Campus
status_detail: AllianceTexas and project sources describe Meta's Fort Worth hyperscale campus as a multi-phase operating data center campus spanning roughly 150-170 acres and about 2.5M sq ft.
notes: No official MW located in reviewed sources; left null.

status_detail: Meta announced Temple in 2022; local coverage says the AI-optimized data center went live in July 2026, and JE Dunn project data lists 152MW across the campus build.
notes: Meta originally described nearly 900,000 sq ft; newer local coverage cites 760,000 sq ft/two buildings as current live phase.

status_detail: Permit coverage reports Microsoft SAT82 as a roughly 244,676 sq ft, $482.6M data center at 18844 FM 157 in Castroville, with construction expected April 2026 to early 2028.

notes: Permit-level details from local tracker/news; retained as separate from SAT82 because location/codenames differ.

status_detail: CyrusOne filed/plans a $500M, 460,000 sq ft data center campus at 3397 US Highway 90 West in Castroville, with completion anticipated June 2027.
notes: Called San Antonio-area in coverage but located in Castroville/Medina County.

status_detail: Riot lists Rockdale as its flagship facility with 700MW of fully approved and energized capacity; 2026 legal/news coverage reports AMD and Anthropic AI/HPC leases tied to the Rockdale site.
notes: Originally bitcoin mining/hosting; being repurposed/leased for AI/HPC capacity.

status_detail: Riot lists Corsicana as operating under 1GW of fully approved and energized capacity for high-density AI/HPC infrastructure.
notes: Riot's page does not provide a specific operational year in the reviewed source.

notes: Cleanview lists operational year 2023; IREN positions the facility for AI/GPU workloads.

notes: Primarily crypto/ASIC compute but included under broad data center superset.

notes: Former Argo crypto mining site converted toward AI/HPC; only current operating building capacity is recorded in capacity_mw.
